summary.title: Writing NES Emulator in Rust
summary.one_liner: A project-based series on building a NES emulator in Rust that can run first-generation NES games, built up through incremental, playable milestones.
keywords: computer systems book elements of computing systems
takeaways: Why the NES is a good target for a first emulator: simple hardware, with a small and straightforward CPU instruction set.
Why Rust suits hardware simulation: low-level control, excellent signed/unsigned and bit-level operations with no overhead.
The series is split into small milestones so that visible, playable progress appears before the emulator is finished.
Prerequisites: basic Rust, bit arithmetic, boolean logic, and binary and hexadecimal numbering.
Recommended references include the Nesdev Wiki, Nerdy Nights, and The Elements of Computing Systems.
summary.summary: This is the introductory page of a written series by @bugzmanov (2020) on building a Nintendo Entertainment System emulator in Rust. It explains the motivation for choosing the NES, the reasons for using Rust (low-level control, efficient unsigned 8-bit and bit manipulation, and performance headroom given that the NES CPU is about 3000 times slower than modern CPUs), and the planned incremental approach. It also lists the prerequisites and a set of reference materials, including the Nesdev Wiki and The Elements of Computing Systems. The page itself is an overview; the implementation chapters are linked from the series.
